findings.message: `fields["owner"] = entry.owner.strip()` writes the model's owner into the composed block without any check. `meta._render` emits `owner: {value}` verbatim, and the only purpose-style check (no newline, no `\r`, no `-->`) is applied to `purpose` alone. A reply owner such as `x\n-->\nanything` therefore ends a `.md` block early and writes arbitrary text into the file. On a `.py` file it adds lines that are not part of the block, so the next `meta refresh` or `check` reports the file as malformed. That breaks the ticket's rule that the model is never given a way to edit a file, and it leaves a written file corrupt.
findings.paved_road: Before writing, validate a nonblank reply owner the same way as `purpose`: reject the entry with a reason such as `invalid owner` when it contains a newline, `\r` or `-->`. Keep the rule that a blank owner is skipped. Add a case to `tests/unit/test_meta_fill.py` showing that such an owner leaves the file byte-identical and lists it as rejected.
